scope: Independent static acceptance of IO-PREREQ Skeleton and RED preparation; production/tests/board read-only

gates.observed_red_assertion_validity: PASS_BY_LOG_AND_SOURCE_REVIEW; fresh execution is parent evidence

findings.description: The adopted design specifies bounded versioned length-prefixed records but leaves precise naming to confirmation. Tests now fix document.ess.eluslot-commit/journal.v1, ELUCOMMIT, payload field order, state byte 1 and ASCII checksum encoding. These are candidate fixture conventions, not a separately frozen exact persistence protocol. The six-file implementation envelope should not silently turn them into architectural persistence decisions.
findings.required_action: Record and review exact private journal/sidecar names, record layout, digest representation, state/checksum binding, limits and malformed handling before production implementation. Do not change tests or approved specification during this acceptance.

findings.description: IO10 only covers expected absent / actual present, not expected present / actual absent. IO12 injects VerifyPublished but not WriteCommittedJournal. IO13 injects Restore but not VerifyRestored. New-file postpublish failure and restored-absence semantics are also not executable. These tests can all turn GREEN while materially violating the adopted contract.
findings.required_action: Add explicit RED cases for both presence directions, commit-record failure, restoration verification failure, and originally absent target rollback; preserve invariants and existing assertions. Test-only follow-up, no product fix in this review.

findings.description: IO15 passes one unframed arbitrary invalid byte string. It does not independently exercise well-framed unknown version, checksum mismatch, valid-checksum traversal/absolute path, target binding mismatch, truncation, maximum/overmaximum journal and path sizes. A decoder that only rejects malformed magic could pass the present test. IO14 tests fail-closed from the same process, not fresh-process reopen as BDD states.
findings.required_action: After private protocol confirmation, create separately malformed fixtures and boundary cases plus independent-process reopen observation. Do not use invalid magic to stand in for all parser safety branches.

findings.description: The helper independently holds a native handle, and after its close/death the parent calls product acquire. This is a valid isolated acquire RED and fixture-health check. It does not prove an actual product-created lease is released on product Drop/process death or that another process can reacquire after product Drop. IO16 therefore only partially maps its intended lifecycle behavior.
findings.required_action: Retain the fixture/native-handle cases and plan separate product lease lifetime/child consumer cases. Do not relabel fixture handle health as product lease behavior.

findings.description: Fixture uniqueness uses process ID and SystemTime nanoseconds without a sequence or collision retry. A coarse or repeated system clock could collide between parallel tests, producing invalid setup rather than intended RED. No collision occurred in reviewed run logs.
findings.required_action: Use an atomic sequence plus exclusive create retry in a later test-only hardening task. Never count any resulting setup error as RED.

findings.location: planning/module-spec.json, envelope.json, test-plan.json and index.html embedded ModuleSpec
findings.description: The canonical planning artifacts still report proposal/review-pending, planning-only envelope and NOT RUN. The later authorization/evidence is separate and real, but automation reading only the ModuleSpec would see a stale lifecycle. Preserve historical decisions while adding an explicit current approval/evidence overlay rather than silently overwriting history.
findings.required_action: Expose the accepted user authority, current Skeleton/RED evidence, and this PARTIAL acceptance in a structured current-state projection.

positive_notes: Ports expose primitive owned data and object-safe traits; no filesystem/OS types escape.
Adapter depends inward on Ports; Windows/std-adapters gate is explicit; no HOST/UI/WORK hookup.
Shipping method bodies explicitly return SKELETON_NOT_IMPLEMENTED; no hidden product commit/rollback algorithm.
Controlled tests compile the same source with cfg(test) ownership/checkpoint constructor; production acquisition is not falsely asserted by fixture lease setup.
Fault tests require actual stage evidence, avoiding accidental PASS from generic Storage errors.
Fixtures validate canonical containment and ownership before recursive cleanup; child is bounded and owned.

suggested_refactors.action: Freeze exact private protocol and lifecycle test scope; do not refactor production during review.
Expand missing contract branches and independent child/product lifecycle tests before READY_FOR_AI_IMPLEMENTATION.
Make fixture naming collision-safe; no broad abstraction or new service needed.

risks.reason: Treating all 20 RED cases as complete module test readiness would leave data-preservation and parser safety branches unspecified/unproved.
Candidate fixture protocol could become accidental persistence SSOT unless frozen explicitly.
Adapter is not wired and intentionally has no behavior; this is a Skeleton acceptance, not deployment readiness.
Evidence host is Windows 10 build 19045; Windows 11 acceptance remains NOT RUN.

review_limits: This reviewer inspected existing source, contracts, feature, fixtures and captured logs but did not rerun Cargo; parent separately executes runtime checks.
Product source, tests and board were not modified by this reviewer.
No recommendation authorizes new product behavior or architectural self-approval.
